current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; your code must check each answer and own the action, review and fallback. As of 1 October 2026, 05:16 UTC, Jev is available to new users: signups have been open since 27 September (TypeSafe CEO's post), new accounts get no free credit, and the API is operational (status page); the pool did not observe signup itself because the console returns HTTP 403. TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output; its published rate limits changed between 29 September 19:24 UTC and 30 September 20:47 UTC to 100K tokens per second and 40 requests per second. OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Opper serve it at the same or rounded list price, while lookalike reseller storefronts charged 3–16× that price. On the six routes whose data terms were read, no primary text allows training on your prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants it a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse, states no retention period and offers zero data retention to enterprise customers, while OpenRouter, Cloudflare and Vercel label the TypeSafe provider zero-retention and Vercel also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, which it marks as not zero-retention (a reading of the text, not legal advice). Published benchmarks, all Reported and graded A–D, disagree because they test different tasks: Jev is usually ahead of cheap LLM setups, close to frontier LLM judges on verdicts that can be read off the text once a threshold is tuned, and behind the best LLMs on derived judgments; TypeSafe's widely quoted 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels. Among open alternatives, only Opper's 362-item test puts one open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev (Opper hosts Kev); JevBench scores Laya and earlier Kev previews well below Jev; Laya's English checkpoint reads about 512 tokens and Kev is English-only. Of five support-ticket triage projects read in source, four send unsure tickets to a person and one files tickets in its archive lane on any Jev API error. Python and TypeScript have official SDKs (typesafe-sdk 0.7.2, @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0); of five Claude Code and MCP guardrails read in source, only LangChain's AutoModeMiddleware fails closed. No audited project or company claim is independently verified as a production deployment.

summary: Access (checked 1 Oct 2026, 05:16 UTC): signups open since 27 Sep 2026, 22:33 UTC (CEO post); no free credit for new users; API operational since 29 Sep, 22:05 UTC (status page). The pool did not observe signup: the console returned HTTP 403.
Jev answers from a fixed answer set: Choice (up to 255 options), Score (up to 10 levels), Noul (probability of yes). It does not generate text and accepts text input only.

List price $0.042/M input, output free on TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare and (in its models API) Vercel; Opper and Vercel's web page round to $0.04; Netlify bills credits. Lookalike resellers displayed 3–16× the list price.

TypeSafe's published rate limits are 100K tokens per second and 40 requests per second; they changed from 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 requests/min between 29 Sep, 19:24 UTC and 30 Sep, 20:47 UTC (Internet Archive captures).

Data handling (quoted 1 Oct, not legal advice): no route's text allows training on prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse; no TypeSafe retention period is stated; ZDR is offered directly to enterprise customers.

Zero data retention by layer: OpenRouter's gateway is ZDR by default and lists the TypeSafe endpoint as ZDR; Cloudflare lists ZDR 'Yes' but AI Gateway logs are on by default; Vercel marks TypeSafe AI ZDR but also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, marked not ZDR; Opper says ZDR is not established for its TypeSafe route.

Jev vs Laya vs Kev: only Opper's 362-item test (B11) puts an open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev, and Opper hosts Kev; JevBench (B07) scores Laya 23.0–41.7 and earlier Kev previews 53.8–59.7 against Jev's 80.0. All Reported.

Laya and Kev weights are Apache-2.0; Kev's Qwen bases are Apache-2.0; Laya's card metadata names no base. Laya's English checkpoint reads 512 tokens and its multilingual checkpoint ships uncalibrated; Kev is English-only.

Support-ticket triage, five projects read at pinned commits: four gate on confidence (0.5–0.9) and send unsure tickets to a person; one ignores queue confidence and archives tickets on API errors; only one validates answers; two set no timeout.

Benchmarks: 14 tier-1 studies and 10 shorter rows graded A–D with flags; all results Reported; the pool ran none. TypeSafe's 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels.

Build: typesafe-sdk 0.7.2; @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 or AI SDK experimental_evaluate (audited at ai 7.0.122; 7.0.126 released 30 Sep, not re-audited). Claude Code and MCP guardrails: only LangChain AutoModeMiddleware fails closed; @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.12.0 (1 Oct) not re-audited.
46 creator videos show Jev running on concrete tasks in 13 use-case groups; seven company and analyst production or cost claims are listed; none is independently verified.
uncertainty: No pool-made Jev call, account, bill or signup; the console returned HTTP 403 on 1 Oct. X could not be searched for newer TypeSafe posts.

TypeSafe's subprocessor list and any SOC 2 report sit behind a script-only trust page and were not read; whether DigitalOcean on Vercel forwards to TypeSafe, and whether OpenRouter's ZDR listing rests on a special agreement, are not stated; Netlify's data terms were not read.
A TypeSafe retention period, human access to inputs and a Telemetry opt-out are not stated in TypeSafe's public text.
Which Kev checkpoints JevBench ran, Kev-9B's base licence, the JevAny/AnyJev identity and the operator of he-jev are unknown.
The five triage projects are code-backed but none is verified as operating; at least 70 more triage repositories were not read.
No benchmark was run or rerun by the pool; four A grades are provisional; no graded comparison with a fine-tuned classifier exists with published materials.
Reddit, X and TikTok could not be read in the daily scan; search analytics were unavailable when page topics were chosen (1 Oct run).
